Plywood export from India runs on a handful of proven lanes, and ours start at Cochin. Containers stuff near the factory and gate in at Vallarpadam ICTT, which keeps inland haulage short and stuffing under our own supervision. Sri Lanka and Israel each have a dedicated lane page; our notes on the Gulf markets are collected under GCC export.

What we export

The range covers the panels a packer, formwork contractor or building-material importer actually orders, not a catalogue of everything with a wood face.

  • Packing-grade MR plywood to IS 303, in 6, 8, 12, 15 and 18 mm as the typical run.
  • Okoume plywood — Okoume is a face veneer on our MR-packing and BWR grades, not a separate grade. We also make calibrated E1 Okoume-face panels on a eucalyptus core; the 16 mm panel weighs about 32 kg and ships bare or HPL-laminated.
  • Film-faced shuttering plywood for formwork.
  • Marine plywood to IS 710 BWP.
  • Plywood boxes and crates, plywood pallets, cable drums and container flooring ply.
  • Sawn timber — rubberwood and jackwood runners for packing work.

Container loading: plywood weighs out before it cubes out

Plywood is dense cargo. A container of packing plywood reaches its permitted payload well before the space is full, so the real question is never "how many sheets fit" — it is how many sheets the box, the shipping line and the destination's road rules will let you carry. Sheets per container is a weight calculation: thickness, panel density, pallet weight and the road limit at the discharge end.

We work both box sizes. A 20ft suits smaller orders and weight-restricted lanes; a 40ft carries more sheets only where the lane's road rules allow the payload, since the cap is on weight, not volume. Loose-loaded and palletised counts differ, and we quote both where it matters. Every export quote carries a loading plan — sheets per container, net and gross weight — so you are not surprised at a weighbridge and you are not paying ocean freight to ship air.

ISPM-15: what actually applies to plywood

This is the most common point of confusion in plywood export from India, so here it is plainly. Plywood panels are exempt from ISPM-15. Plywood is a processed wood material, manufactured under heat and adhesive pressure, so the panels themselves need no stamp and no fumigation at any border that follows the standard.

What ISPM-15 does cover is solid-wood packaging — the sawn-timber runners and battens inside boxes, crates and pallets. Our box and crate process is ISPM-15 compliant, so packaging that includes solid-timber components ships with treatment already handled. If you are weighing treatment routes for your own packaging, our note on heat treatment versus methyl bromide covers the difference.

Terms, documents and turnaround

Export quotes are in USD, FOB Cochin by default. Payment is 50% advance with the balance before dispatch for standard products, and 100% advance for custom specifications. We accept bank transfer (T/T).

Each shipment sails with the documents stated on the proforma invoice — commercial invoice and packing list as standard, with a treatment certificate or phytosanitary certificate where the destination, product or contract requires one, and a certificate of origin where the destination requires it. Nothing waits for the vessel to leave.

To get a quote moving, send thickness and sheet size, grade or face veneer, quantity, and the destination port. A reply comes within one business day from sales@cochinwood.in, or call +91 95674 10175.

export/australia.before: Customs duty[RATE TO CONFIRM] — we do not publish a destination rate. Your broker confirms the Australian tariff line for your sub-heading and the rate in force.
export/australia.after: Customs dutyThe general (MFN) Australian customs duty for plywood under HS 4412 is 5% ad valorem under Schedule 3 of the Customs Tariff Act 1995, with a handful of narrow sub-lines — such as bamboo plywood and blockboard/laminboard/battenboard — already Free. Under the Australia–India Economic Cooperation and Trade Agreement (ECTA), in force since 29 December 2022, HS 4412 sits in Staging Category A in Australia’s schedule, meaning the tariff was eliminated on entry into force. Plywood from India that qualifies as originating under the ECTA Rules of Origin, and travels with a valid Certificate of Origin, therefore clears at 0% rather than the 5% general rate; without that certificate the 5% MFN rate applies instead. Ask your broker to confirm the exact 8-digit tariff line and that no separate anti-dumping or countervailing duty measure applies, since Australia runs active anti-dumping measures on plywood from some other origins.

export/australia.before: GST at import[RATE TO CONFIRM] — charged on the customs value plus customs duty and other incidental import charges, not on CIF alone.
export/australia.after: GST at importGST at import is a flat 10%, with no reduced or exempt rate for plywood or other timber products. It is calculated on the Value of the Taxable Importation (VoTI) — the customs value of the goods, plus any customs duty payable, plus the cost of international transport and insurance to Australia — not on CIF value alone. This is the standard formula the Australian Border Force and Australian Taxation Office apply to all commercial imports, and GST is payable at the same time and in the same manner as customs duty, generally at clearance.

export/australia.before: Typical transit[TRANSIT TO CONFIRM] — this site does not publish a Cochin-to-Australia port-to-port figure. It is a deep-sea voyage in the 21-day-plus band; ask the export desk against the routing your forwarder books.
export/australia.after: Typical transitNo carrier or forwarder publishes a Cochin-specific port-to-port sailing time to Australia, since the lane runs exclusively via transshipment — typically through Colombo, Port Klang or Singapore, as no direct service exists on this route. Published figures for comparable Indian gateways span roughly 15 days to Fremantle up to around 22 days to Melbourne or Sydney from ports such as Nhava Sheva and Visakhapatnam, with door-to-door timelines commonly quoted at 20–30 days once pre- and on-carriage are included. That puts Cochin squarely in the 21-day-plus deep-sea band this site already flags, with Fremantle typically the fastest Australian port of call from India and Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane a few days longer; ask the export desk to confirm the current figure against the routing your forwarder books, since it varies by carrier and transshipment port.

export/chile.before: Customs duty[TO CONFIRM] — no Chilean duty or tax figure is stated anywhere on this site, and none is guessed here. Your clearing agent confirms the tariff line and the rates in force.
export/chile.after: Customs dutyChile applies its general (MFN) customs duty of 6% ad valorem on the CIF value for plywood under HS 4412 — the India–Chile Preferential Trade Agreement (in force since 2007, expanded 16 May 2017) is a positive-list agreement, and plywood is not among the wood-chapter lines Chile has offered India a preference on, so the flat MFN rate applies with no antidumping or safeguard surcharge layered on top. IVA (VAT) is charged separately at 19% on the customs value plus duty. A broader India-Chile trade agreement (CEPA) is under negotiation but not yet in force, so it has no bearing on the rate payable today. Your clearing agent confirms the exact tariff line and the rate in force at the time of entry.

export/chile.before: Plant health / biosecurity[TO CONFIRM] — ask your agent before you order whether the entry needs an import permit, an additional declaration or a phytosanitary certificate. We issue fumigation and phytosanitary certificates where the destination requires them, confirmed against your country's rules at proforma-invoice stage, but the requirement has to reach us before production ends.
export/chile.after: Plant health / biosecurityFor manufactured plywood, Chile’s SAG (Servicio Agrícola y Ganadero) treats the standard production process — veneer peeling, kiln-drying, gluing and hot-pressing — as sufficient treatment in its own right, placing plywood in Category 1 under Resolución Exenta No. 1.284/2021. Category 1 goods do not require a phytosanitary certificate, import permit or additional declaration at entry, so none is needed for the panels themselves, provided the commercial invoice and packing list clearly describe the process, since SAG inspectors retain discretion to request documentation. This exemption covers the plywood cargo only: any wood packaging used to ship it (pallets, crating, dunnage) is separately subject to Chile’s standard ISPM-15 heat-treatment and stamp requirement, the same as almost every destination. We confirm packaging and any country-specific requirement against your order at proforma-invoice stage.

export/germany.before: Customs duty[RATE TO CONFIRM] — we do not publish a destination rate. Your broker confirms the EU tariff line for your sub-heading and the rate in force.
export/germany.after: Customs dutyThe EU Common External Tariff charges 7% ad valorem on the customs value for the general plywood lines under HS 4412.31–.39 that Indian gurjan- and keruing-faced plywood normally falls under, where the outer ply is not one of the specifically named tropical species — confirmed directly in the EU TARIC database against CN 4412 31 90 00 and CN 4412 33 90 90, both at 7.00% (Reg. 1549/2006 and Reg. 1821/2016). India does not currently benefit from any FTA or GSP reduction: the India–EU trade agreement was concluded on 27 January 2026 but remains unratified and is not yet in force, so the standard third-country rate applies in full. No anti-dumping duty touches India-origin plywood — the EU’s 86.8% anti-dumping duty on hardwood plywood targets China only. Your clearing agent confirms the exact 10-digit CN code for your specific species and construction, since a named-species outer ply (okoumé, meranti, mahogany and others) or a birch-faced panel falls under a different line with its own rate.

export/germany.before: VAT at import[RATE TO CONFIRM] — Einfuhrumsatzsteuer is charged on the customs value plus customs duty, not on CIF alone.
export/germany.after: VAT at importEinfuhrumsatzsteuer is charged at Germany’s standard VAT rate of 19% — there is no reduced 7% rate for plywood or other manufactured wood panels; the reduced-rate wood entry in Anlage 2 UStG (item 48) covers only firewood and sawdust or wood waste, not HS 4412 products. The assessment basis is the customs value plus the customs duty (§11 UStG), not CIF alone, so Einfuhrumsatzsteuer works out to (customs value + 7% customs duty) × 19% for this shipment.

export/haiti.before: Customs duty[TO CONFIRM] — no Haitian duty or tax figure is stated anywhere on this site, and none is guessed here. Your clearing agent confirms the tariff line and the rates in force.
export/haiti.after: Customs dutyHaiti does not apply the CARICOM Common External Tariff, even though it has been a CARICOM member since 1999 — the CET was never enacted into Haitian law, and Haiti instead runs its own national MFN tariff schedule, set by annual finance-law decree and generally lower than the CARICOM bands. That schedule’s overall simple average is 4.9% of CIF value, and the wood products group covering HS 4412 plywood averages roughly 4.5–4.8%, ranging 0–20% depending on the specific line; published tariff databases (WTO, UNCTAD/WITS, ITC Market Access Map) do not break out the exact ad valorem rate for HS 4412 itself, so this is the one figure to pin down before quoting a landed cost. Three further charges apply to CIF value on top of whatever that duty turns out to be: a 5% preshipment verification fee collected via SGS, a 10% TCA turnover tax (Haiti’s VAT equivalent, charged on CIF value plus duty plus the inspection fee), and a 2% CFGDCT local-development contribution. Your clearing agent confirms the exact HS 4412 duty rate in force alongside these three additional charges.

export/kenya.before: Customs duty and import taxes[TO CONFIRM — Edwin] The site has never published a rate for this lane and one is not invented here. Duty and any import tax are set by the destination tariff schedule against the line your goods are classified under, and applied at import. export/kenya.after: Customs duty and import taxesKenya applies the EAC Common External Tariff to plywood imports from India: HS 4412 covers every plywood, veneered-panel and laminated-wood construction (bamboo plywood, ordinary plywood up to 6mm ply, LVL, blockboard/laminboard/battenboard, and other), and it sits in the CET’s intermediate-goods band at 25% ad valorem on CIF value — not the 35% top band, which is reserved for finished and sensitive goods such as wooden frames, packing cases and furniture. India has no free-trade or tariff-preference agreement with Kenya or the EAC, so this standard CET rate applies in full with no reduction to claim. export/puerto-rico.before: Customs duty[TO CONFIRM] — no duty or tax figure for Puerto Rico is stated anywhere on this site, and none is guessed here. Your customs broker confirms the tariff line, the rate in force, and which customs regime the entry falls under.
export/puerto-rico.after: Customs dutyPuerto Rico sits inside US customs territory, so a direct India–Puerto Rico plywood shipment is dutied exactly like a mainland US entry, under HTS Chapter 4412. The base (Column 1/MFN) rate for the tropical hardwood-faced plywood typical of Indian commercial and marine ply runs 8% ad valorem on lines such as 4412.31, 4412.33, 4412.34 and 4412.51/.52 — India holds no US FTA or GSP preference, so 8% is the floor for this shipment, though a handful of coniferous-faced lines run lower and birch-faced panels are typically duty-free, and only your customs broker can confirm the exact 8/10-digit line. On top of the base rate: the Section 232 timber/lumber tariff (10% on softwood lumber, effective 14 Oct 2025) explicitly excludes HTS 4412 plywood, including lauan-faced panels, so it does not apply here, though Commerce is due to report to the President by 1 Oct 2026 on whether to extend Section 232 to hardwood products; and the IEEPA ‘reciprocal tariff’ on India, along with the Section 122 surcharge that briefly replaced it, are both no longer in force — the Supreme Court struck down the IEEPA tariffs on 20 Feb 2026, and the Section 122 surcharge lapsed by around 24 Jul 2026. A separate Section 301 action against forced labour, covering 60 economies including India, took effect 24 Jul 2026 at a 10% ad valorem surcharge on goods not covered by its exclusion list — but published sources disagree on whether wood products sit on that exclusion list, so whether the 10% reaches this shipment is unresolved; have your broker confirm the current Section 301 status of the specific HTS line before costing the order, since it is the difference between roughly 8% and roughly 18% total federal duty. Separately from the federal duty, and regardless of how the Section 301 question resolves, Puerto Rico’s own Impuesto sobre Ventas y Uso (IVU) applies to goods brought onto the island at a combined 11.5% (10.5% Commonwealth plus 1% municipal), administered by the Departamento de Hacienda via an Import Declaration (Model SC 2970) filed through the SURI portal on every shipment; this is the Puerto Rico buyer’s liability rather than CWI’s as FOB seller, and a buyer holding an Eligible Reseller Certificate can defer it and collect IVU on resale instead of paying it at the port.
